localChanges: Civilization II games now fight with Civilization II's combat: units have hit points and firepower, battles run over several rounds, damage stays until a unit heals, a damaged unit moves more slowly, winners can become veterans, aircraft run out of fuel, Triremes can be lost at sea and SDI Defense stops nuclear attacks nearby; the computer players weigh their attacks by the new odds (#1007).

In Civilization II games, the unit card shows a unit's hit points, its firepower and, for an aircraft, the turns of fuel it has left, and a damaged unit has a small health bar over it on the map (#1007).

Civilization II's new orders have keys and buttons: Transform (O), Build Fortress (F), Build Airbase (E), Paradrop (P), which then takes a click on the square to drop on, and Airlift (L), which lists the cities the unit can reach. Long-pressing or right-clicking a square in reach offers them too (#1007).
In Civilization II games, pillaging a square with more than one improvement now asks which one to take, and a Spy next to a lone enemy unit can sabotage it (#1007).

In Civilization II games, you're now told when one of your units is promoted to veteran after a win, runs out of fuel, or is shot down while being airlifted, and when SDI Defense stops a nuclear attack (#1007).
Battles in Civilization II games now play the battle sounds, as Civilization's do: the sword, the gun or the bombing run, by the unit (#1007).
In Civilization games, computer players no longer treat a Carrier as a troop ship: a Carrier holds only aircraft (#1007).
In both games, you're now told when one of your cities loses population because its defender was defeated.
In the game setup, Civilization II's combat handicaps for the easier levels are listed by name, and can be switched off (#1007).

A resolver's result must name the attacker and defender as winner and loser and leave the winner alive, or the attack throws `CombatResultError` and changes nothing. A `NaN` defender score ranks last. The single roll is unchanged.

With neither registered, an attack is the same single roll as before, with the same two draws in the same order. With a resolver, the winner keeps the damage it took and `Damaged` is processed for it, the loser is `Defeated`, and a winning attacker spends its power as before.

Characterisation tests for `Attack.perform`: two draws, the attacker's first, a tie to the attacker, power spent only on a win, and the strongest defender (the first of equals). The workflow now installs with pnpm, checks formatting, recompiles and runs the tests, like core-unit's.

An optional `distance(target, cityTile)` measures the radius, by default `Tile#distanceFrom`, for a ruleset whose radius counts something other than straight-line distance (Civilization II's `map_distance`).

`movedRules`' `coastBoundLoss` can be a function of the unit and the tile it ended on, so a ruleset can change the odds by advance or wonder; a chance of 0 draws nothing and loses nothing. A number keeps today's single draw.
A new `nearLand` option says what is in sight of land (by default the tile is on the coast, as before), and `adjacentToLand` is the test where the tile or any neighbour is land.
`protectedByCityWithin(cityRegistry, radius, protects)` builds a detonation `vetoes` from the cities within a radius of the target, for a defence such as Civilization II's SDI Defense.
The comment said no `CanStow` rule would accept anything; with none applying, `canStow()` is true for any unit, so only the zero capacity protects it. A test pins that.

The Submarine now extends `NavalTransport`, so a ruleset can give it a hold (Civilization II's submarines carry missiles). A ruleset that gives it no `Capacity` and no `Carries` trait, as Civilization I's doesn't, sees it carry nothing: it saves and sends exactly what it did, and a Submarine from an older save gets its transport collaborators when the game loads it.

Moves the package to the pnpm workflow the other engine packages use (prettier check, compile with a stale-output check, tests), drops the yarn and npm lock files, and adds tests pinning what a Submarine is today: a naval unit that saves and sends exactly what any naval unit does.

A unit carries `_damage` in a save only while it is damaged, so saves of games without damage are unchanged.
The CombatResolver, DefenderRank and WorkRate docs now say that a rule declines through its criteria, that only one should match, and what a resolver's result must be.

A unit's damage is stored only while it is damaged (`damage()`, `setDamage()`, `hitPoints()`), so units that never take any save and checksum exactly as before. `DelayedAction` takes `ceil(turns / rate)` turns when a `WorkRate` rule answers, and the turns given otherwise. Nothing changes for a game that registers none of the new rules.

A naval transport type the ruleset gives nothing to carry (no `Carries` trait) is no longer sailed to waiting passengers, built or researched as a ferry, counted as a way overseas, waited for by aircraft, or sailed by barbarians. Every transport Civilization I declares carries something, so its games play as before; this is for the Submarine, which becomes a naval transport so that Civilization II's can carry missiles (civ-clone/web-renderer#1007).

A Carrier carries aircraft, not passengers, so in every ruleset, Civ1's included, computer players no longer sail one to waiting passengers, count it as room for them, or count it when choosing a transport to build or research.

A missile (`SingleUse`) is spent in its attack, so it attacks whatever it has the fuel to reach, with no need to get back. A damaged aircraft with no fuel to bring it back (Civ2's Helicopter, which loses hit points outside a city or airbase) heads for a city to heal as a land unit does, and rests on an Airbase as in a city.

In a ruleset with battles in rounds (a `CombatResolver`, as in Civ2), passengers are ferried, and transports built, researched and counted as room for them, only by a ship whose `Carries` trait takes land units, so the Carrier and Civ2's Submarine, which carries missiles, are never sailed to waiting passengers or counted as room for them. Elsewhere (Civ1) transports are chosen as before.

An aircraft whose ruleset gives it a Fuel range (Civ2) moves and attacks only where it can still reach one of its player's cities or carriers before its fuel runs out, by base-unit-fuel's `fuelState`. Civ1's aircraft, and Civ2's Helicopter, are judged as before.

A unit with damage (only a ruleset that deals it, such as Civ2, has any) rests while it is in one of its player's cities or on a Fortress, and below half its hit points heads for the nearest city, preferring one with Barracks, a Port Facility or an Airport for its kind. It never leaves a city to do so.

Where a ruleset fights battles in rounds with hit points and firepower (a `CombatResolver` is registered, as in Civ2), a computer player works out its chance of winning from base-combat-rounds' `combatOdds`, at the terms the battle would be fought at, and attacks only at 0.6 or better, or 0.25 or better against an enemy next to one of its cities. Without a resolver (Civ1), attacks are weighed as before.

A Spy sabotages only a unit worth at least half its own cost, or one that can attack and stands next to one of its player's cities. Paradrops, airlifts, fortresses, airbases and terrain transforms are never taken as a step.
